certificate.title: Certificate of Erasure
certificate.statement: This certifies that all records associated with the subject identified below have been rendered permanently unreadable by destruction of their subject key.
certificate.boundary_notice: Crypto-shredding covers data encrypted by this system. Plaintext exported to spreadsheets, analytics pipelines, or email before deletion is not covered by this certificate.
threat_model.title: Threat Model
threat_model.scope_intro: Keyring protects data at rest against database and backup compromise, and enforces per-subject crypto-shredding. It does not, by itself, protect against the following.
threat_model.boundary.live_compromise: Live server compromise with keys resident in process memory at the time of compromise.
threat_model.boundary.authz_bugs: Application authorization bugs in systems that call this API with valid credentials.
threat_model.boundary.root_admin: A root-level administrator on the host, database, or provider backend.
threat_model.boundary.compromised_client: A compromised client application holding valid operator credentials.
threat_model.boundary.exported_plaintext: Plaintext already exported to spreadsheets, analytics pipelines, email, or logs before a destroy or erasure operation.
threat_model.closing: Documenting this boundary is part of the design, not an appendix to it. A system marketed as comprehensive protection generates false confidence more dangerous than no encryption.
